title: Direct guest harness runtime and guest workload control
objective: Install and run the model-agnostic Little Mester harness directly inside the outer VM guest, with native guest auth and broad guest-level control. Docker/Compose are available to the agent for arbitrary project workloads; no Docker container wraps the agent. Preserve the outer VM host-isolation boundary and existing restricted egress/secret rules.

acceptance_criteria.text: A selected harness (initially OpenCode) is installed and launched as a native guest process in the VM, not as a Docker container; it opens the TUI in the invoking session and operates on the selected workspace.

The guest agent can use Docker CLI and Compose against the guest daemon to start, inspect, stop and remove a representative project service (including PostgreSQL) and run tests in a repeated feedback loop.

Guest authority is documented accurately: the agent can administer its guest and guest Docker; this is not treated as host isolation. No host Docker socket, host filesystem outside the selected workspace, host credentials, or LAN access is exposed.

Guest Docker/Compose supports ordinary project workflows without a restrictive generated wrapper silently rewriting compose files or blocking normal guest-local service ports; guest workloads remain inside the outer VM boundary.

Nested VM support is explicitly tested: report host KVM nested VMX/SVM capability, guest CPU virtualization flags and /dev/kvm availability, then boot and stop a nested test VM. Unsupported hosts report a clear limitation; no nested support is claimed without a live pass.

Existing harness checks that apply to direct guest execution (verify-lab, TUI exit-confirm, metrics/model connectivity where configured) pass, and the same runner interface can select another supported harness without changing the VM trust boundary.
OpenCode version selection/update is reproducible and updates guest software without destroying the VM overlay or workspace; credential state is preserved or exported/imported through the #45 flow.

OpenCode update procedure: select version, rebuild/pull agent image only (not VM/base), prove installed version changes despite Docker cache; normal relaunch does not rebuild/re-download CLI; credential export/import or persistent data survives replacement (#45).

created: tests/vm.bats: pinned semantic-version validation, direct guest CLI installation path and interactive `lab-vm agent` command wiring.
tests/vm.bats: confirms `lab-vm agent` checks installed OpenCode version/config and does not invoke installer or config sync.
tests/vm.bats covers the guest config install/launch path agreement, flat /etc/opencode/opencode.json location, and version output parsing without escaped-quote awk failure.
cases: 2026-10-28 prerequisite feedback: real CachyOS guest boots and installs Docker packages but rootless installer fails on unloaded nf_tables. #41 now loads/persists the guest module and sets service drop-in before installer starts Docker; no rootful or --skip-iptables fallback. Agent CLI/daemon capability AC remain pending until live guest verification. Existing ./lab compose has GPU-local model dependencies, so running it unmodified inside CPU-only VM is not evidence of #42 completion.

2026-10-28 owner asks whether every OpenCode update needs a rebuild: current agent/Dockerfile npm-installs @opencode/cli into the image; container root is read-only. Current updates require replacing/rebuilding agent image, not full VM provisioning. Plain builds may reuse cached npm layer; no automatic version-refresh path is implemented. Version selection/targeted update remains pending A8. No image rebuild or session restart performed.

Implementation started 2026-10-28 after architecture reconciliation commit 2ba3773: `lab-vm up` now provisions OpenCode natively in guest OS with a pinned version (default 2.2.0), syncs project config/plugins, rewrites local model endpoints to the existing guestfwd host API, and no longer invokes the Docker agent-image build in the up path. Existing running VMs take the same idempotent install path without overlay recreation. `lab-vm agent [name]` attaches an SSH TTY and execs OpenCode in /workspace as mester with guest proxy/Docker environment. New Bats cases cover version pin guard and command wiring. Local validation: full Bats 75/75, VM Python tests 12/12, docs 110/110, shell syntax and git diff --check pass. No live KVM/guest runtime available in this workspace; direct TUI, auth, Docker Compose and nested KVM remain unverified.

Follow-up correction 2026-10-28: user clarified setup should install defaults once, not require the `agent` launch command as an install step. `lab-vm up` remains the installation/repair path; `lab-vm agent` now only checks installed version/config and opens the TUI. Repeated agent launches no longer reinstall or sync config. Local regression test added; live guest check pending.

Host feedback 2026-10-28: `lab-vm up` installed Node/npm and OpenCode but failed at sed because config was extracted to /etc/opencode/opencode.json while code referenced /etc/opencode/opencode/opencode.json. `lab-vm agent` then failed because its awk program contained literal escaped double quotes. Fixed config references to the actual extracted path; replaced launcher version parsing with grep -Eo; normalized version comparison in installer so an already-correct version does not reinstall on each up. Existing VM/overlay is preserved. Re-run `./lab-vm up --debug --unsafe-recurse --auto-accept` to repair/sync in place, then `./lab-vm agent`; no `down`, `stop`, or clean operation.
